o.text: Morphologically from sönmək (“to go out (of light etc.)”) + -dür. Cognate with Turkmen and Turkish söndürmek, Kazakh сөндіру (söndirüw), Uzbek so'ndirmoq.

From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (qonuq). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kon- (“spend the night”), whence also Azerbaijani qonşu (“neighbour”). Compare Turkish konuk (“guest”), Crimean Tatar qonaq (“meeting room”), Chuvash хӑна (hăna, “guest”).

From Old Anatolian Turkish تخيل (taxïl), from Arabic دَخْل (daḵl).
Doublet of dəxl.
From Proto-Common Turkic *tēr-. Cognate with Turkish dermek.
Borrowed from Arabic يَوْم الخَمِيس (yawm al-ḵamīs).
